changes.before: If, after reviewing the scenarios above, you still believe your refund amount contains an error, you may file a Protest to dispute CBP’s refund decision upon liquidation or reliquidation.
changes.after: Should you disagree with the calculation of your IEEPA refund, you retain the right to file a protest under 19 U.S. C. § 1514, contesting the liquidated or reliquidated IEEPA refund amount. Filing a timely protest will keep the liquidated or reliquidated IEEPA refund amount from becoming final and will provide an opportunity to submit additional information or corrections for liquidated/reliquidated entries as needed. To ensure that CBP has complete and accurate information, please check your entry records and confirm that all information, including the duty, classification, and value information for each entry summary line, was correctly declared in accordance with the CBP Form 7501 instructions and CSMS messaging, and please explain and correct any errors you believe to exist in the documentation supporting your timely protest. To be timely, a protest contesting the liquidated or reliquidated IEEPA refund amount must be filed within 180 days after the date of liquidation or reliquidation. Regardless of whether a protest is filed, if CBP discovers an error in the liquidation/reliquidation of an entry with an IEEPA refund, CBP will aim to reliquidate the entry within 90 days from the date of the original liquidation. However, due to the volume of entries involved, and the need for agency-wide consistency in the exercise of its voluntary reliquidation authority with regard to IEEPA refunds, the Centers of Excellence and Expertise will not be responding to questions regarding the liquidated or reliquidated IEEPA refund amounts received for specific entries, other than by processing a timely filed protest contesting the liquidated or reliquidated IEEPA refund amount. IEEPA refund-related inquiries that do not concern, or are not limited to, the liquidated or re-liquidated IEEPA refund amount received for specific entries may be directed to IEEPARefunds@cbp.dhs.gov .
changes.engine: Engine unchanged: protest window stays 180 days (19 U.S.C. 1514); PSCs and protests on entries in an accepted declaration remain blocked until liquidation. Engine unchanged: 90-day voluntary reliquidation limit.

changes.before: Yes, at least for entries in Phase 1, which covers unliquidated entries and entries within the 90-day voluntary reliquidation period. Liquidation constitutes the final assessment of duties on an entry for all purposes, and a voluntary reliquidation within the 90-day period may correct any error in the original liquidation. CAPE processing removes all IEEPA tariffs from an entry. Nonetheless, entries are still subject to any duties, taxes, and fees, including pursuant to other trade remedy provisions, that are applicable upon liquidation or reliquidation within the 90-day period. It is possible to receive a bill after CAPE processing if the amount paid on the entry as a whole is less than the recalculated duty owed at liquidation or reliquidation. As with all refunds issued by CBP, CBP will check for any unpaid debts owed to CBP by the IOR before issuing the refund, and the refund (or bill) amount will be equal to the difference between the IEEPA duties to be refunded and the amount owed on an entry-by-entry basis.

It is the responsibility of the trade community to ensure that the information provided on the CBP Form 5106 is accurate and complete. Importers and other entities can update their CBP Form 5106 using two methods: Licensed Customs Broker: A licensed customs broker with a valid Power of Attorney (POA) can submit updates on an importer’s behalf using Action Code U (Update) in the Automated Broker Interface (ABI). Through the ACE Portal: Importers can update their information directly using the web-based ACE Secure Data Portal. The portal also allows users to run reports, respond to CBP forms, create declarations, and manage accounts. To use the ACE Portal, your company must first set up an account and grant user access. Learn more at Apply for an ACE Portal Account . To prevent processing delays, please ensure that all required data fields on the CBP Form 5106 are fully and accurately completed when submitting an update.

changes.before: ACE Portal users with Importer sub-account access can monitor refund activity using ACE Reports. The REV-603 Trade Refund report covers successful refunds. The REV-613 ACH Rejected Refunds report highlights any refunds that have been rejected due to the recipient not being enrolled in ACH Refunds. For help with refund reports, review the ACE Refund Report training guide . For more information about rejected refunds, see Replacement Refund Instructions .

changes.before: All refunds are required to be paid electronically via Automated Clearing House (ACH) (Federal Register Document 2025-24171 ). To receive a refund, CBP must have your bank information on file. If bank information designated for refunds is not on file with CBP, the refund will not be paid until that information is provided through the ACE Secure Data Portal (ACE Portal). See more information at ACH Refund Enrollment Overview .
